questions.q: What does a binding let a CRM Analytics dashboard do?
options: Bind a dataset to a Salesforce object permanently
Let one part of a dashboard read a value from another step and use it
Lock a dashboard so nobody can edit it
Convert a dashboard into a recipe
questions.explain: Bindings connect steps and widgets, so a selection or a query result in one place can drive what another shows.

questions.q: Which kind of binding is driven by what the user picks in a filter, toggle, or chart, and is re-evaluated whenever that choice changes?
questions.explain: Selection bindings follow user interaction. Results bindings read the results of another step's query.

questions.q: In the SAQL binding example, what do the double curly braces indicate?
options: A JSON array of literal text
An expression that CRM Analytics evaluates rather than literal text
questions.explain: Double curly braces mark a binding expression. Functions like column and cell inside them pull values from other steps.

questions.q: A dashboard text label should show a default of "All" when the user has selected nothing. Which function is often used to supply that default?
questions.explain: coalesce returns the first non-empty value in its list, so it can fall back to "All" when a selection binding is empty.

questions.q: Besides query filters, where can bindings be used, according to the lesson?
options: Widget text and widget properties, such as a reference line's value, as well as inside SAQL
Nowhere else; bindings work only in filters
questions.explain: Bindings can feed filters, text, widget properties like a reference line's value or label, and SAQL. Always verify current syntax in the documentation.
